items.question: Why are you interested in Cloudflare's Software Engineering Internship? What products or features are you interested in building?
items.problem:
Expected "Most of what I build runs against real users or real traffic, so infrastructure that has to work every time is the kind of problem I want to spend time on. Cloudflare routes traffic for millions of properties, which means correctness and failure modes matter more than any individual feature being clever.

The closest analogue in my own work is the job-application agent I built in TypeScript and Node with Playwright. The whole design question was where automation should stop. I used SQLite as the single source of truth because browser automation gets dangerous when state diverges across processes, put every mutating capability behind fail-closed flags that never default on, and made free-text and demographic fields architecturally impossible to autofill. I also built a validation ladder so a capability is not called working just because it passes against a local fixture.

What I would want to build at Cloudflare is developer-facing platform work: APIs, edge services, and the tooling around them. I have shipped a versioned FastAPI microservice and public detection API with CI scaffolding for an anomaly-detection system, plus an LLM explanation layer over retrieval, and I would like to do that kind of work at much larger scale."; page shows "Undergrad"
